title: Kestrel and the Portrait
premise: True-crime podcaster Vesper Joubert has spent five years cataloguing the unsolved disappearance of town founder Edmund Kestrel, whose portrait still hangs in the courthouse. When Kestrel's grave is opened for a historical survey and the coffin proves empty, Vesper discovers the exhumation was ordered by someone using forged papers — and that the town's founding families have been paying into a private fund for a century to keep one secret buried. Following the money, Vesper uncovers that Kestrel faked his own death to escape prosecution for a murder he committed, and that his descendants have been hiding him in plain sight ever since: the 'caretaker' of the Kestrel estate is Edmund himself, kept alive by complicity and fear. In the end, Vesper must choose between exposing the truth and destroying the found family of townsfolk who protected the lie to survive — and they choose truth, broadcasting the confession Edmund makes on tape before his actual death three days later.
about_author: Gideon Whitlock is the pen name of a former small-town newspaper reporter who spent a decade covering courthouses, cemeteries, and the people who haunt both. He writes mysteries about places that keep their secrets too well.

chapters.title: The Empty Box
chapters.summary: Vesper Joubert attends the public exhumation expecting closure for their podcast's flagship episode; instead the coffin holds only century-old bricks. POV Vesper. The beat is cold shock — five years of careful filing collapse when the case refuses to stay closed.

chapters.title: Alphabetized Secrets
chapters.summary: Vesper reviews their archive and finds the exhumation permit was signed with a dead clerk's signature. Town archivist Marisol Vega, Vesper's closest friend, warns them off. POV Vesper. The beat is unease: the first hint that someone inside Vesper's trusted circle knows more than they're saying.

chapters.title: Portrait of a Founder
chapters.summary: Studying the courthouse portrait, Vesper notices the painting was restored recently — over an older image showing Kestrel with a scarred left hand. The current Kestrel heir, Aldous, dismisses them brusquely. POV Vesper. The beat is obsession tightening its grip as the podcast becomes personal.

chapters.title: The Hundred-Year Ledger
chapters.summary: Vesper traces a shell charity funded by the founding families since 1924, its disbursements going to a single unnamed recipient. Someone ransacks their studio overnight. POV alternating Vesper and an anonymous ledger-keeper's diary entries. The beat is dread — the conspiracy is generational and patient.

chapters.title: What Marisol Buried
chapters.summary: Marisol confesses her grandmother was the diary-keeper and that the families paid hush money after Kestrel allegedly murdered a labor organizer. She begs Vesper to stop. POV Marisol. The beat is heartbreak: love against duty, as friendship strains under inherited silence.

chapters.title: The Caretaker
chapters.summary: Following the ledger's payments, Vesper reaches the crumbling Kestrel estate and meets its elderly caretaker — a man with a scarred left hand who quotes Edmund Kestrel's speeches verbatim. POV Vesper. The beat is vertigo: the coldest case on record just walked into the room.

chapters.title: Confession at Dusk
chapters.summary: The caretaker admits he is Edmund, dying now of heart failure, and offers the full truth on tape if Vesper will let him die unprosecuted. Vesper records it but cannot promise anything. POV Vesper. The beat is moral crisis — power corrupted even in its final hours, bargaining with the truth.

chapters.title: Aldous Moves First
chapters.summary: Aldous, learning of the recording, tries to have Vesper silenced and the estate burned; Marisol takes a beating shielding the tapes, and the town finally sees what its respectability cost. POV Marisol. The beat is fury and resolve — the found family chooses each other over the founders.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Vesper airs the confession live from the courthouse steps beneath Kestrel's portrait, naming the murder, the fund, and every family that paid. Edmund dies that night before any warrant can issue. POV Vesper. The beat is catharsis laced with grief — truth won, but no justice will follow.

chapters.title: The New Portrait
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the town votes to replace the founder's portrait with one honoring the murdered organizer; Vesper and Marisol hang it together, the podcast ending its run. POV Vesper. The beat is quiet restoration — some families are chosen, and some stories are finally allowed to rest.
